I've built the simulator in `output/` (C++20, standard library only). `cmake -B build && cmake --build build` builds it cleanly into `build/gcode_simulator`, and it supports every option you listed.

**Testing:** I ran the three trace examples from your requirements and matched them: the G81 times 0.3 / 0.42 / 3.42 / 3.72, and the H99 error giving exit 1 with `error_line_number: 2`. I also ran the canned-cycle test program from Appendix C of the spec in all three planes, plus small programs for cutter compensation, arcs (full-circle, helical, negative R), inverse-time feed, rotary-only moves, probing (trip and no-trip), G92/G10/G28/G30, M6, M2/M30 resets, parameter expressions, `%` files, block delete and the command-line error cases. These were checks by eye; there is no automated test suite.

**Things that may surprise you:**
- **`G1 F60` on its own line is an error.** The spec says G0/G1 with no axis words is an error, so I follow it. Plenty of real programs do this, so it's the behaviour most likely to trip you up.
- **The spec's own cutter compensation example (Table 12) fails.** Your clarification says I/J are measured from the tool-tip position. After the spec's entry move, the tip isn't where the example assumes, so line N0030 fails the arc-radius check. A typical contour (straight entry, outside corners, arcs) works.
- **Inside (concave) corners under cutter compensation are an error.** This follows the NIST reference interpreter (the spec is NIST's RS274NGC), which only rounds outside corners and doesn't handle inside ones.
- **`machine_position` moves when G43/G49 changes the tool length offset**, even with no motion. I treat it as the tool tip's position, so G43 H1 with length 2.0 lowers Z by 2.

**Where the spec was silent, I chose:**
- **Startup modes:** G0, G17, G90, G94, G20, G40, G49, G98, G54, G64, plus M5, M9, M48. G98 comes from your G81 example.
- **Carousel and tool table:** 68 slots by default, as the spec states. With no `--tool-table`, every

editorial.last_message: Claims broad simulator support after manual examples, not automated conformance tests. Three failures expose G-code tolerance, required rotary parameters and already-tripped probing.
